---
title: "10 - Summary statistics for the text and supplementary figures"
output: html_document
---

**Purpose.** Generates one-off numbers that are reported in the text of the
paper (database size, plot counts, percentages, etc.), two supplementary
tables, two figures, and the site-level data for the map figure, none of
which are produced elsewhere in the pipeline:

- the Chapman-Richards parameter illustration (`c-r_curve_example_fig.png`)
- the agroforestry category x Audebert climate region matrix (`af_cat_aud_reg_matrix.png`)
- site-level carbon CSVs used to draw the site map

**Inputs.**

- `data/groa_af/studies.csv`, `sites.csv`, `measurements.csv` (GROA-AF dataset)
- `output/intermediate/s3_by_plot.xlsx` (notebook 01)
- `output/intermediate/soc_data_out_c_t_ha_norm_30.xlsx` (notebook 02c)
- `output/data/*_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx` (notebooks 03a/03b)
- `output/data/*_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx` (notebook 04)
- `output/tables/agc_cr_fit_table_filtered.xlsx` (notebook 07)

**Outputs.**

- `output/tables/agc_cr_fit_table_filtered_w_trees_per_ha.xlsx`
- `output/tables/bp_and_parkland_prior_cat_summary.xlsx`
- `output/tables/sites_with_{agc,bgc,soc}[_change]_for_map.csv`
- `output/figures/c-r_curve_example_fig.png`
- `output/figures/af_cat_aud_reg_matrix.png`

Each section below is independent once the setup chunk has been run.


# Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(ggrepel)

# Single-category agroforestry codes used throughout the analysis. Plots
# assigned to multiple categories (e.g. "AC, SA") are excluded where this
# filter is applied.
af_cats <- c('AC', 'BP', 'COP', 'FAL', 'FOD', 'MS', 'OTH_AF', 'PAR', 'RB',
             'ROT', 'SA', 'SP', 'SPC', 'TMC', 'WL')

read_groa <- function(table) read.csv(here("data", "groa_af", paste0(table, ".csv")),
                                    na.strings = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM",
                                    colClasses = c(study_id = "character", site_id = "character", plot_id = "character"))
s1 <- read_groa('studies')
s2 <- read_groa('sites') |> rename(ecoregion = audebert_ecoregion_5class)
s3 <- read_groa('measurements')

read_int <- function(file) read.xlsx(here("output", "intermediate", file))
read_data <- function(file) read.xlsx(here("output", "data", file))

# Before outlier removal (notebooks 03a/03b)
agc_w_covars <- read_data('agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx')
bgc_w_covars <- read_data('bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx')
soc_w_covars <- read_data('soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars.xlsx')

# Final analysis datasets (notebook 04)
agc_final <- read_data('agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx')
bgc_final <- read_data('bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx')
soc_final <- read_data('soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx')

# Final datasets restricted to single, listed agroforestry categories
agc_df <- agc_final |> filter(af_cat %in% af_cats)
soc_df <- soc_final |> filter(af_cat %in% af_cats)
```


# Database and dataset sizes

Unique plots are distinct study/site/plot combinations. The measurements table stores these as
separate columns; the plot-and-age tables store them pre-combined as
`ssp_id` ("study_id;site_id;plot_id"). Studies and sites are literature- and
site-level, so a plot count doesn't apply.

```{r database-row-counts}
n_unique_plots_s3 <- s3 |> distinct(study_id, site_id, plot_id) |> nrow()

pools <- list(
  agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars = agc_w_covars,
  bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars = bgc_w_covars,
  soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars = soc_w_covars,
  agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers = agc_final,
  bgc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers = bgc_final,
  soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers = soc_final
)

pool_counts <- tibble(
  metric = paste(names(pools), "rows"),
  n = map_int(pools, nrow),
  n_unique_plots = map_int(pools, \(d) n_distinct(d$ssp_id))
)

bind_rows(
  tibble(
    metric = c('sites rows', 'measurements rows', 'studies rows with included == 1'),
    n = c(nrow(s2), nrow(s3), sum(s1$included == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_unique_plots = c(NA, n_unique_plots_s3, NA)
  ),
  pool_counts[1:3, ],
  pool_counts[1:3, ] |>
    summarise(metric = 'sum of agc + bgc + soc w_covars rows',
              across(c(n, n_unique_plots), sum)),
  pool_counts[4:6, ],
  pool_counts[4:6, ] |>
    summarise(metric = 'sum of agc + bgc + soc w_covars_drop_outliers rows',
              across(c(n, n_unique_plots), sum))
)
```


# Plot counts by Audebert climate region

Share of all plots (measurements table) falling in each ecoregion.

```{r audebert-region-plot-counts}
s3_plots <- read_int('s3_by_plot.xlsx')
audebert <- s2 |> select(site_id, ecoregion)

s3_plots |>
  left_join(audebert |> select(site_id, ecoregion), by = 'site_id') |>
  mutate(ecoregion = na_if(trimws(ecoregion), '')) |>
  count(ecoregion) |>
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```


# Plot counts by agroforestry category (all pools combined)

A plot can appear in more than one pool (and at more than one age). Each
plot is assigned a single category, preferring the category recorded at a
non-zero age.

```{r comb-af-cat-plot-counts}
bind_rows(agc_final, bgc_final, soc_final) |>
  filter(af_cat %in% af_cats) |>
  group_by(ssp_id) |>
  summarise(
    af_cat = {
      non_zero_age_cats <- unique(af_cat[age != 0])
      if (length(non_zero_age_cats) > 0) non_zero_age_cats[1] else unique(af_cat)[1]
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  count(af_cat, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```


# Tree density and AGC by agroforestry category

Medians by category, plus a pooled row for the low-stature systems
(fallow, fodder bank, coppice) and an overall row.

```{r agc-af-cat-summary}
summarise_density <- function(d) {
  summarise(d,
            n = n(),
            trees_per_ha_median = median(trees_per_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
            c_t_ha_median = median(c_t_ha, na.rm = TRUE))
}

bind_rows(
  agc_df |> group_by(af_cat) |> summarise_density() |> arrange(desc(trees_per_ha_median)),
  agc_df |> filter(af_cat %in% c("FAL", "FOD", "COP")) |> summarise_density() |>
    mutate(af_cat = "FAL + FOD + COP"),
  agc_df |> summarise_density() |> mutate(af_cat = "Overall")
)
```


# Tree density added to the AGC Chapman-Richards fit table

Adds mean and median tree density for each region x category row of the
AGC fit table (notebook 07).

```{r agc-biomass-table-tree-density}
# Two header rows and line breaks in long header/cell text (07): read from the
# second row and restore the plain labels ("(Sub)tropical" -> "Tropical/subtropical")
read_cr_table <- function(file, sep.names = ".") {
  d <- read.xlsx(file, startRow = 2, sep.names = " ")
  unwrap <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("\\s*\\r?\\n\\s*", " ", gsub("/\\r?\\n", "/", x))
    x <- sub("^All cats\\.$", "All AF categories", x)
    sub("^Insuff\\. data$", "Insufficient data", sub("^\\(Sub\\)tropical", "Tropical/subtropical", x))
  }
  names(d) <- gsub(" ", sep.names, unwrap(names(d)), fixed = TRUE)
  d[] <- lapply(d, \(x) if (is.character(x)) unwrap(x) else x)
  d
}
agc_biomass_table <- read_cr_table(here("output", "tables", "agc_cr_fit_table_filtered.xlsx"))

# Map each fit-table Region label to the ecoregion values it
# aggregates over (NULL = no filter, i.e. all regions including NA)
region_map <- list(
  "Tropical/subtropical wet" = c("Tropical/subtropical wet"),
  "Tropical/subtropical dry" = c("Tropical/subtropical dry"),
  "Tropical/subtropical all" = c("Tropical/subtropical wet", "Tropical/subtropical dry"),
  "Temperate wet"            = c("Temperate wet"),
  "Temperate dry"            = c("Temperate dry"),
  "Temperate all"            = c("Temperate wet", "Temperate dry"),
  "Boreal/polar"             = c("Boreal/polar"),
  "All ecoregions"           = NULL
)

# "All AF categories" rows aggregate over every category in agc_df
subset_for_row <- function(region, af_cat_val) {
  d <- agc_df
  regs <- region_map[[region]]
  if (!is.null(regs)) {
    d <- d[d$ecoregion %in% regs & !is.na(d$ecoregion), ]
  }
  if (af_cat_val != "All AF categories") {
    d <- d[d$af_cat == af_cat_val, ]
  }
  d
}

agc_biomass_table <- agc_biomass_table |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    trees_per_ha        = mean(subset_for_row(Region, AF.category)$trees_per_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    trees_per_ha_median = median(subset_for_row(Region, AF.category)$trees_per_ha, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(
    'Tree density, mean (stems Ha\u207b\u00b9)'   = trees_per_ha,
    'Tree density, median (stems Ha\u207b\u00b9)' = trees_per_ha_median
  )

write.xlsx(agc_biomass_table,
           here("output", "tables", "agc_cr_fit_table_filtered_w_trees_per_ha.xlsx"),
           overwrite = TRUE)
```


# Prior land use for boundary plantings and parklands

For plots of a given category, tallies how many (and what %) list each
prior land-use category. `prior_land_use` is a comma-separated string, so a plot
with several prior categories counts toward each and percentages need not
sum to 100.

```{r prior-cat-summary-by-af-cat}
summarize_prior_cats <- function(df, df_name, af_cat_val) {
  sub_df <- df |> filter(af_cat == af_cat_val)
  n_sub <- nrow(sub_df)

  sub_df |>
    mutate(prior_land_use = if_else(prior_land_use == "" | is.na(prior_land_use),
                                "None listed", prior_land_use)) |>
    separate_longer_delim(prior_land_use, delim = ", ") |>
    count(prior_cat = prior_land_use, name = "n_plots") |>
    mutate(df = df_name, pct_of_plots = round(100 * n_plots / n_sub, 1)) |>
    select(df, prior_cat, n_plots, pct_of_plots) |>
    arrange(desc(n_plots))
}

# One row per prior category, AGC and SOC side by side as "n (%)"
build_prior_cat_table <- function(af_cat_val) {
  bind_rows(
    summarize_prior_cats(agc_df, "AGC", af_cat_val),
    summarize_prior_cats(soc_df, "SOC", af_cat_val)
  ) |>
    mutate(label = paste0(n_plots, " (", pct_of_plots, "%)")) |>
    select(df, prior_cat, label) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = df, values_from = label, values_fill = "0 (0%)") |>
    rename(`Prior land use` = prior_cat) |>
    arrange(desc(AGC))
}

bp_prior_cat_table       <- build_prior_cat_table("BP")
parkland_prior_cat_table <- build_prior_cat_table("PAR")

knitr::kable(bp_prior_cat_table, align = "lcc", caption = "BOUNDARY_PLANTING")
knitr::kable(parkland_prior_cat_table, align = "lcc", caption = "PARKLAND")

write.xlsx(
  list(BOUNDARY_PLANTING = bp_prior_cat_table, PARKLAND = parkland_prior_cat_table),
  here("output", "tables", "bp_and_parkland_prior_cat_summary.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

```{r soc-gra-prior-by-af-cat}
soc_gra <- soc_df |>

bind_rows(
```

## Boundary planting / riparian buffer plots vs. all other categories

Mean of each numeric covariate by group, and the most common levels of key
categorical covariates among BP/RB plots.

```{r soc-bp-rb-vs-other-covariates}
soil_tex_cols <- soc_df |> select(starts_with("soil_tex_"), -soil_texture_class) |> names()
loam_cols <- soil_tex_cols[str_detect(soil_tex_cols, "loam")]

bp_rb_df <- soc_df |>
  mutate(grp = ifelse(af_cat %in% c("BP", "RB"), "BP/RB", "Other")) |>
  # NA in these one-hot soil texture columns means absence
  mutate(across(all_of(soil_tex_cols), ~replace_na(.x, 0))) |>
  mutate(soil_tex_any_loam = as.numeric(rowSums(across(all_of(loam_cols))) > 0))

numeric_vars <- bp_rb_df |> select(where(is.numeric), -row_id) |> names()

bp_rb_df |>
  group_by(grp) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(numeric_vars), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  pivot_longer(-grp, names_to = "variable", values_to = "mean") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = grp, values_from = mean) |>
  mutate(diff = `BP/RB` - Other) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(diff)))

for (v in c("ipcc_reg", "ecoregion", "soil_texture_class", "country")) {
  cat("\n---", v, "---\n")
  print(
    bp_rb_df |>
      filter(grp == "BP/RB") |>
      count(.data[[v]], sort = TRUE) |>
      mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
      head(4)
  )
}
```

## Share of plots with a diachronic (repeated-measurement) design

`soil_comparison` (from notebook 02c) classifies how each SOC comparison was
built. `plot_change` means the same plot was resampled and compared to its
own earlier reading (strict diachronic definition). `plot_change/site_ref`
also resamples the same plot but compares it to a separate non-AF site
reference (broader definition). All other values are control or
chronosequence comparisons.

`soil_comparison` isn't kept in the final SOC dataset, so it is pulled from the
intermediate output, with the same `sc_flag == ''` filter used in notebook
04a, and restricted to plots in the final dataset (all categories).

```{r soc-diachronic-pct}
soc_comp_lookup <- read_int('soc_data_out_c_t_ha_norm_30.xlsx') |>
  filter(sc_flag == '') |>
  distinct(ssp_id, soil_comparison)

final_soc_plots <- unique(soc_final$ssp_id)

# Every final plot should have a soil_comparison classification
stopifnot(all(final_soc_plots %in% soc_comp_lookup$ssp_id))

matched_soc_comp <- soc_comp_lookup |> filter(ssp_id %in% final_soc_plots)

tibble(
  definition = c(
    'plot_change only (plot resampled, compared to its own earlier reading)',
    'plot_change + plot_change/site_ref (plot resampled, compared to own reading or a site reference)'
  ),
  n_diachronic_plots = c(
    sum(matched_soc_comp$soil_comparison %in% 'plot_change'),
    sum(matched_soc_comp$soil_comparison %in% c('plot_change', 'plot_change/site_ref'))
  ),
  n_total_plots = nrow(matched_soc_comp),
  pct_diachronic = round(100 * n_diachronic_plots / n_total_plots, 1)
)
```


# Figure: Chapman-Richards parameter illustration

Illustrates how each parameter of $y = a(1 - e^{-bt})^c$ shapes the curve,
varying one parameter at a time around a = 10, b = 0.5, c = 2.

```{r cr-curve-example-fig, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
cr_fun <- function(t, a, b, c) a * (1 - exp(-b * t))^c

t_vals <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 400)

vary_param <- function(values, param_name, panel_label) {
  map_dfr(values, function(v) {
    args <- list(a = 10, b = 0.5, c = 2)
    args[[param_name]] <- v
    tibble(t = t_vals,
           y = do.call(cr_fun, c(list(t = t_vals), args)),
           param = paste0(param_name, " = ", v),
           panel = panel_label)
  })
}

df_plot <- bind_rows(
  vary_param(c(5, 10, 15),      "a", "Varying a \n (upper asymptote)"),
  vary_param(c(0.25, 0.5, 1.0), "b", "Varying b \n (growth rate)"),
  vary_param(c(1, 2, 3),        "c", "Varying c \n (curve shape)")
)

# One label per curve, placed at the sampled point nearest t = 2.5 / 5 / 7.5
t_targets <- c(2.5, 5, 7.5)

df_labels <- df_plot |>
  group_by(panel) |>
  group_modify(~ tibble(param = unique(.x$param),
                        t_target = t_targets[seq_along(unique(.x$param))])) |>
  left_join(df_plot, by = c("panel", "param")) |>
  group_by(panel, param, t_target) |>
  slice_min(abs(t - t_target), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(panel, param, t_lab = t, y_lab = y, label = param)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = t, y = y, color = param)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = df_labels,
    aes(x = t_lab, y = y_lab, label = label, color = param),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3, label.size = 0.25, label.r = unit(0.1, "lines"),
    label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"), fill = "white", alpha = 0.9,
    box.padding = 0, point.padding = 0.1, min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.alpha = 0.5, seed = 123
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Carbon stock",
       title = "Effects of a, b, and c on the Chapman-Richards curve")

ggsave(here("output", "figures", "c-r_curve_example_fig.png"),
       width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 600)
```


# Figure: agroforestry category x Audebert climate region matrix

Number (and row %) of plots in each category x climate region combination,
based on all plots in the measurements table (before carbon-pool-specific filtering). Plots with
multiple categories contribute one row per category. Regions with 30 or
fewer plots are omitted.

```{r af-cat-aud-reg-matrix, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
# Categories shown in the figure (FOD, OTH_AF, PAR, RB and ROT are not shown)
matrix_af_cats_plot <- c('AC', 'BP', 'COP', 'FAL', 'MS', 'SA', 'SP', 'SPC', 'TMC', 'WL')

# Ecoregions from the sites table (includes nearest-zone assignments)
site_regions <- audebert |>
  select(site_id, ecoregion) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character),
         ecoregion = na_if(trimws(ecoregion), ''))

af_cat_reg_df <- s3_plots |>
  left_join(site_regions, by = "site_id") |>
  separate_longer_delim(af_cat, delim = ', ') |>
  # Unassigned plots would inflate the n labels but are dropped from the cells
  filter(af_cat %in% matrix_af_cats_plot, !is.na(ecoregion))

reg_order <- af_cat_reg_df |>
  count(ecoregion, name = "reg_n") |>
  arrange(desc(reg_n)) |>
  mutate(reg_lbl = paste0(ecoregion, '\n(n = ', reg_n, ')')) |>
  filter(reg_n > 30)

af_cat_reg_df <- af_cat_reg_df |>
  filter(ecoregion %in% reg_order$ecoregion)

cat_order <- af_cat_reg_df |>
  count(af_cat, name = "af_cat_n") |>
  arrange(af_cat_n) |>
  mutate(af_cat_lbl = paste0(af_cat, '\n(n = ', af_cat_n, ')'))

af_cat_reg_df |>
  count(af_cat, ecoregion) |>
  na.omit() |>
  group_by(af_cat) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(cat_order, by = "af_cat") |>
  left_join(reg_order, by = "ecoregion") |>
  mutate(reg_lbl    = factor(reg_lbl, levels = reg_order$reg_lbl),
         af_cat_lbl = factor(af_cat_lbl, levels = cat_order$af_cat_lbl)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = af_cat_lbl, x = reg_lbl, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_label(aes(label = paste0(n, ' (', round(pct, 1), '%)')),
             size = 3.5, fill = "white", alpha = 0.6, label.size = 0) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

ggsave(here("output", "figures", "af_cat_aud_reg_matrix.png"), height = 5, width = 9)
```


# Site-level carbon data for the site map

Mean carbon stock (plots aged 5 years or more) and mean annual carbon change
per site, joined to site coordinates and area. One CSV per pool and metric.

```{r map-site-csvs}
site_data <- s2 |>
  transmute(site_id,
            lat_min = bbox_lat_min, lat_ctr = lat, lat_max = bbox_lat_max,
            lon_min = bbox_lon_min, lon_ctr = lon, lon_max = bbox_lon_max,
            area_m_sq = area_ha * 1e4, area_ha) |>
  drop_na()

site_means <- function(df, value_col, out_name, min_age = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(min_age)) df <- df |> filter(age >= min_age)
  df |>
    mutate(site_id = str_split(ssp_id, ";", simplify = TRUE)[, 2]) |>
    group_by(site_id) |>
    summarise("{out_name}" := mean(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    left_join(site_data, by = "site_id") |>
    na.omit()
}

for (pool in c("agc", "bgc", "soc")) {
  stock  <- get(paste0(pool, "_final"))
  change <- read_data(paste0(pool, "_change_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))

  write.csv(site_means(stock, "c_t_ha", pool, min_age = 5),
            here("output", "tables", paste0("sites_with_", pool, "_for_map.csv")))
  write.csv(site_means(change, "c_t_ha_yr", paste0(pool, "_change")),
            here("output", "tables", paste0("sites_with_", pool, "_change_for_map.csv")))
}
```
